judgementRule: A passage is relevant when it states the answer the query asks for, in the language the query is written in, on its own — a paragraph that only answers in the context of the file around it is not judged relevant, because chunk retrieval is what is being measured. The corpus was authored for this measurement, so relevance is judged by construction: the relevant paragraph is the paragraph written to answer the query. A passage stating the same fact in another language is not counted for that query: the backend is a lexical signature and is not cross-lingual, and counting it would measure the judgement instead of the retrieval.
labelFormat: corpus-relative source path + '#' + the chunk locator the index produced, read from corpus-manifest.json
nature: Synthetic fixture text. The operator's own research corpus is not measured here.
